newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Abiove raises soybean import estimate.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Abiove raises soybean import estimate.

text.p: Brazilian soybean imports are now expected to reach 1.3 million tonnes in the 1996/97 commercial year (February/January), according to the Brazilian Association of Vegetable Oils Industries (Abiove).
This is up from an August forecast of one million tonnes and well above last year's 791,000 tonnes.

In a revised estimate, it also increased its forecast for soybean exports to 3.6 million tonnes from 3.4 million in August. The new figure means Abiove now expects slightly higher exports than the 3.52 million tonnes shipped last year.

Abiove also upwardly revised its soymeal production and export estimates, with some 10.4 million tonnes now expected to be shipped overseas against a previous 10 million tonnes. However, this is still well below last year's 11.54 million.
In addition, Abiove now estimates that Brazil will actually import soymeal for the first time - but only 100,000 tonnes.

"It has never happened before....but this year with no tariff for imports from Mercosul countries, some companies have decided it is worth their while to import from Argentina and Paraguay," an Abiove official said.
The soymeal is expected to arrive from now to the end of the year, the official said.
The new supply and demand estimates follows.
All figures are in thousands of tonnes. SOYBEANS 1996/97(Oct) 1996/97(Aug) 1995/96
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
